package_info.package_name: N/A (timing attack on npm private packages)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of private packages (potentially affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack exploits a timing side-channel vulnerability in the npm registry API to enumerate the existence of private package names. This enables attackers to discover confidential package names, which can then be used to create malicious clones or typosquatted packages, increasing the risk of targeted supply chain attacks against organizations.

execution_context.file_location: N/A (external API request to npm registry)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends repeated GET requests to the npm registry API for specific package names, measures the HTTP response times for 404 errors, and analyzes timing differences to infer the existence of private packages.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it systematically probes the npm registry for package names and leverages subtle timing differences in 404 responses to enumerate private packages, which is not a legitimate or documented use of the API.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal usage would involve checking for public package existence or downloading packages, not inferring private package names through timing analysis of error responses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use may include checking for public package availability before publishing, but not automated enumeration or timing-based inference of private package existence.
key_indicators: Automated, high-frequency GET requests to the npm registry for package names
Measurement and statistical analysis of HTTP response times for 404 errors
Targeting of organization-scoped or likely-private package namespaces (e.g., @organization/*)
Absence of actual package download or install actions

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends repeated GET requests to the npm registry for candidate package names, measuring response times for 404 errors.
attack_chain.leads_to: Identification of private package names used by the target organization.

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers a public package with the same or similar name as the discovered private package (typosquatting or direct impersonation).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is available publicly under a name trusted by the target organization.

attack_chain.action: Target organization or its developers accidentally install the malicious clone, leading to potential supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: Automated enumeration of package names via npm registry API using repeated GET requests
Analysis and correlation of HTTP response times for 404 errors to infer package existence
Burst or pattern of requests targeting organization-scoped package namespaces (e.g., @organization/*)
Lack of follow-up actions such as package download or install after enumeration
file_indicators: N/A (attack is external and does not leave file artifacts on the target system)
network_indicators: High-frequency GET requests to https://registry.npmjs.org/ for non-existent or private package names
Patterns of requests targeting @organization/* package namespaces
Unusual volume of 404 responses correlated with specific timing analysis
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for automated or high-frequency GET requests to the npm registry for package names, especially those matching internal or organization-scoped patterns (e.g., @organization/*). Detect clients that measure and analyze HTTP response times for 404 errors to infer package existence. Alert on attempts to register public packages with names similar to known private packages, and correlate enumeration activity with subsequent suspicious package registrations.
